author: Samuel Stubbs
title: Connor Zilisch didn't want to do Justin Marks wrong while looking for new opportunity - NewsBreak
text:
By Samuel Stubbs ,
49 minutes ago
Connor Zilisch. Connor Zilisch won't be behind the wheel of the No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet until 2028, but he can rest easy over the next 16 months without worrying about his future.
Zilisch, who was officially signed by HMS on Tuesday after news of the pairing broke on Monday , will continue to drive for Trackhouse Racing through the end of the 2027 campaign before moving to Hendrick.
"It's been a few months of talking and figuring things out," Zilisch said Wednesday on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio. "I've been very open with (Trackhouse Racing owner Justin Marks) through the entire process, and Justin's been great to me since the day I met Justin and got to work with him and be with Trackhouse Racing.
"I didn't want to treat him wrong. I didn't want to leave with a sour taste in either of our mouths. I certainly appreciate Justin and the way he's handled everything. A few months ago, I let Hendrick know I was going to be available in 2028. I knew that Alex (Bowman) was close to the end of what he wanted his career to be."
Why Connor Zilisch signed with Hendrick now Zilisch knew that Kyle Larson, William Byron and Chase Elliott are at HMS for the long haul. He didn't hesitate to sprint through the proverbial open door that opened with the news that Bowman would retire at the end of 2027.
"When that seat opens up, I want to try and fill myself in there," Zilisch said, "Because I know if not, the opportunity's not going to be there anytime soon. It's certainly something I'm really excited about. I obviously have a year and a half left with Trackhouse and a lot of work left to do.
"We've started to make some gains. I want to make sure that I continue to work hard, I continue to try to get the most out of my team, make sure that we go out on a high note."
